red.focus: Separate legally material facts from background detail
red.summary: An effective legal analysis identifies which facts change the outcome under a rule. Learn to recognize a real injury while avoiding irrelevant narrative detail.
checklist: I can identify a fact that affects a legal element
I can separate evidence of harm from moral indignation
I can write a concise issue statement

sections.title: Facts Are Not All Equal
sections.body_md: A client reports that a driver was rude, wore a blue jacket, and ran a red light before striking a pedestrian. The jacket may be irrelevant, the insult may matter to the human experience, and the red-light violation may be legally significant. A material fact changes how an applicable rule is applied. To identify it, first find the rule and its elements. Then ask which pieces of the story establish or undermine a required condition. That is the beginning of useful legal analysis.

sections.title: Harm Must Be Legally Located
sections.body_md: A client may feel betrayed after a broken promise, but a remedy depends on the legal claim and its rules for loss or injury. The lawyer should listen respectfully while distinguishing emotional reaction, factual loss, and legally recognized harm. Some legal systems protect emotional injury in defined circumstances; others require particular proof or limits. A clear issue statement does not erase the client's experience. It turns the experience into questions a court or other institution can actually decide.

sections.title: Use a Materiality Test
sections.body_md: Write each asserted fact on a line and ask: if this were different, might the governing rule produce a different answer? If yes, the fact may be material. If not, it may be useful context or irrelevant. Materiality also depends on disputed defenses and remedies, so do not discard a fact before identifying the whole legal issue. A concise account should preserve what affects law, evidence and client welfare without repeating details that cannot alter the analysis.

yellow.focus: Analyze materiality through elements and defenses
yellow.summary: Move beyond identifying significant facts to organizing conflicting evidence. Learn to explain how the same fact may matter differently to duty, breach, causation or a defense.
checklist: I can map material facts to claim elements
I can identify a missing fact that could change the outcome
I can distinguish favorable evidence from conclusive evidence

sections.title: Build a Fact-to-Element Map
sections.body_md: A visitor slips in a shop. A photograph shows water on the floor, an employee's log shows a recent inspection, and the claimant says no warning sign was visible. The photograph can prove a condition existed but may not show how long it existed. The log may support reasonable care or invite a question about what inspectors actually saw. Each fact should be mapped to the applicable duty and breach standards. One compelling image does not prove every required legal element.

Each fact should be mapped to the applicable duty and breach standards. One compelling image does not prove every required legal element.

sections.title: Defenses Change the Map
sections.body_md: If the governing law permits a comparative-fault defense, the claimant's conduct may become material even though it does not erase the defendant's potential wrong. Evidence concerning warning, visibility, or avoidability could matter. But the defense and its allocation of proof depend on jurisdiction. The lawyer must not import a defense from another system merely because it sounds familiar. Add the defense as a separate set of elements and ask which facts support or weaken it.

The lawyer must not import a defense from another system merely because it sounds familiar. Add the defense as a separate set of elements and ask which facts support or weaken it.

sections.title: Write a Fair Statement of Uncertainty
sections.body_md: A witness remembers the spill, but video footage begins after the fall. The uncertainty concerns how long the spill existed and whether the shop had a legally required opportunity to address it. The strongest analysis states that uncertainty explicitly and identifies evidence that could resolve it. Overstating what a photograph or witness proves may persuade briefly but weakens the reliability of legal advice. Clear thinking distinguishes possible, probable and legally established facts.

orange.focus: Evaluate contested fact patterns and inferential strength
orange.summary: Analyze cases with inconsistent testimony and incomplete records. Distinguish legal proof from a coherent story and identify alternative explanations that must be tested.
checklist: I can evaluate competing narratives against the actual evidence
I can distinguish credibility from corroboration
I can identify when a fact supports multiple explanations

sections.title: A Coherent Story Can Be False
sections.body_md: A witness offers a detailed account of a crash, but the physical traces support only parts of it. A legal analyst must distinguish internal consistency from external corroboration. Memory, incentives, conditions of observation and later information may affect testimony. The weight a tribunal gives this evidence follows the governing rules, not simply a personal impression that a speaker seems confident. A structured analysis states each disputed proposition, the evidence bearing on it, and the strongest competing explanation.

sections.title: One Fact, Several Inferences
sections.body_md: An employee deleted messages shortly after receiving a legal complaint. The timing might support an inference of concealment, but alternative explanations could exist, including routine retention practices. The analyst must identify which inference the law permits and what foundation is required. An adverse inference should never be treated as automatic merely because the conduct appears suspicious. The larger skill is proportional inference: conclusions should be no stronger than the evidence and applicable doctrine justify.

sections.title: Materiality Includes Process
sections.body_md: Some facts matter to whether a case can be heard, not to whether a wrong occurred. A filing deadline, signed notice, or jurisdictional connection may decide procedure before a tribunal examines injury. A mature fact map separates threshold questions, substantive elements, defenses, remedies and credibility. This structure prevents the writer from conflating a likely moral wrong with a legally viable case. It also guides investigation toward the missing fact most likely to change the outcome.

black.focus: Critique fact construction and structural invisibility in adjudication
black.summary: At doctoral depth, examine how institutions determine which harms and evidence count as legally relevant. Develop methods that make excluded perspectives visible without relaxing standards arbitrarily.
checklist: I can identify how legal categories shape visible injury
I can evaluate evidentiary asymmetries affecting vulnerable parties
I can defend reforms that preserve reliable proof and fair notice

sections.title: Legal Categories Can Hide Harms
sections.body_md: A worker experiences repeated low-level discriminatory actions, none of which seems decisive alone. A doctrine focused only on isolated events may fail to capture cumulative experience, while a pattern-based test may recognize it under applicable law. The analyst must not simply assert that every unfair act constitutes a legal violation. The doctoral question is how the governing rule defines an actionable pattern, what evidence supports it, and whether the rule's categories reflect the actual problem the law aims to address.

sections.title: Evidence Is Unequally Held
sections.body_md: An employer may control internal messages and data needed to establish a claim while the worker has only personal records. Procedural disclosure, presumptions, protective orders and confidentiality safeguards can alter that imbalance, where authorized. The institutional choice matters: unlimited disclosure can invade third-party privacy and produce burdens, while strict proof rules can make valid rights unreachable. A principled reform identifies the facts truly necessary and allocates access and cost proportionately.

sections.title: A Defensible Theory of Materiality
sections.body_md: A doctoral proposal should not treat every socially meaningful fact as legally decisive. It should specify the protected interest, relevant pattern, evidence standard and safeguards against false attribution. Invite affected people to describe harms while preserving the right of others to challenge allegations. The art of legal reasoning is to create accurate, reviewable pathways from experience to a legal conclusion. Sensitivity and rigor are complementary when the law is meant to protect real human beings.
